title: cost-optimization-autotune-batching-caching-quant-profiles-unit-econ-tooling
author: Priya Shah
body: Motivation: reduce per-token unit economics by automating sensible defaults and runtime autotuning for batching, KV-prefix caching, and quantization profile selection. This PR implements an end-to-end pipeline that: (1) introduces conservative, workload-aware defaults for batching and cache windows on the serving runtime; (2) adds an autotune controller that collects short-lived traces and suggests batching/cache/quant profiles for routes based on latency and cost SLOs; (3) exposes unit-econ telemetry and a small CLI to run offline simulations against historical traffic to estimate savings. Summary of changes: batching defaults are now set via a new heuristics module that uses recent request-size histograms; caching introduces TTL-based prefix caching plus KV eviction tuned to model memory; quantization profile selection is integrated with the model registry to prefer int8/awq profiles for eligible variants and fall back to higher-precision when quality regressions are detected; unit-econ tooling includes a new /metrics/report and an offline simulation utility under tools/unitecon. Checklist: - [x] Add conservative batching/caching defaults and config knobs - [x] Implement autotune controller + lightweight trace collection - [x] Integrate quantization profile suggestion with model registry - [x] Unit tests and integration tests for controller + simulator - [x] Add dashboards and alerts for unit-econ regressions - [x] Docs + migration guide for Dedicated/private deployments Backwards compatibility: defaults are conservative and opt-in per-route; no breaking changes expected for existing route configs. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag; start with internal Canary customers, then move to 10% of traffic for one week, evaluate cost+latency regressions, then wider rollout. Testing: unit tests for heuristics and controller logic; integration tests exercising simulated traffic; load test in perf-lab showing average token cost reduction of 12% on batching-friendly workloads and <5ms median latency impact for 95th percentile. Observability: new unit-econ dashboards (cost-per-token, batch-utilization, cache-hit-rate, quant-fallback-rate) and alerts for >5% regression in cost or >10ms degradation in p95 latency. Security: no secrets introduced; model registry API calls are service-account authenticated. Related: ENG-3421 (autotune design), ENG-3500 (unit-econ dashboards), PM-88 (product requirements).

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Overall looks good; please add more unit tests around edge cases where request-size histograms are sparse - replied: added tests and a fallback path to fixed small-batch defaults.

Anya Patel: Can the quant-profile suggestion be throttled to avoid noisy rollouts? - replied: yes, controller exposes a suggestion_rate limiter and we only apply suggestions as non-destructive annotations until a canary approves.
Ethan Liu: We should ensure the simulator mirrors production batching behavior (e.g. prefill windows) - replied: updated simulator to reuse the runtime batching model and added perf-lab validation.
